This application coming on for admission this day, the   the following:
 ORDER
This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail.

The applicant apprehends his arrest in connection with Crime No.RC2222022A0004 registered at Police Station CBI-Bhopal for the offence punishable under Sections 381,420,467,468,471 of IPC and Sections 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(a) of Prevention of Corruption Act,1988, and Section 66(C)of I.T. Act.

The allegation against the present applicant is that while being posted as Assistant in the Post Office in the year 2020, he misappropriated the funds by manipulating the electronic records, and in this way defalcated an amount of Rs.13,85,771/-, causing huge loss to the post office.

sentences.text: Shri Ankit Saxena, learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has already deposited the entire amount under protest to show his bona fide.

It is stated that the application before the trial Court was merely dismissed on the ground that he failed to appear before the Special Court on 10.01.2023 nor filed any application or medical certificate on that day.

It is contended by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant came to Bhopal on 10.01.2023 from Gwalior, and on that day, the train was late and he was also suffering from high fever so he immediately met with doctor,
who advised him to take bed rest, and issued certificate which is also annexed to this application as Annexure A/5.
However, the learned Special Court has failed to consider the aforesaid document.

He has relied on decisions of Apex Court in Aman Preet Singh vs. C.B.I.Through Director (Criminal Appeal No.929/2021, arising out of SLP (Crl.)No.5234/2021), dated 2nd September, 2021 , and Siddharth vs. The State of U.P. and Another (Criminal Appeal No.838/2021, arising out of SLP (Crl.)No.5442/2021), dated 16th August, 2021.

sentences.text: It is submitted that since all the record is before the authority concerned and the applicant has already deposited the entire amount, allegedly, defalcated by him, and no further custodial interrogation is required, the applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.
Per contra, Shri Singh, learned counsel appearing for the CBI has vehemently opposed the bail application.
He has also raised the question regarding the maintainability of this application.
Shri Singh has further stated that power under Section 438 Cr.P.C.is an extra ordinary remedy and has to be exercised sparingly.

Reference is made to the case of Vijay Mandal Choudhary and others vs.
U.O.I.and others Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.4634/2014, wherein in para 83, the Supreme Court has held that grant of anticipatory bail at the stage of investigation may frustrate the investigating agency in interrogating the accused and in collecting the useful information and also the material which might have been concealed.

sentences.text: Success in such interrogation would elude if the accused knows that he is protected by the order of the Court.

In view of Full Bench decision rendered on 30th September, 1994 in the case of Nirbhay Singh and another vs. State of M.P. 1995 (0) MPLJ 296, the question regarding maintainability of the application is over ruled.

sentences.text: Considering that the applicant has already deposited the entire amount, alleged to be defalcated by him, and as further custodial interrogation of applicant is not required, without adverting to the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rs. One Lakh Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the arresting officer.

It is further directed that the applicant shall also comply with the provisions of Section 438(2) of Cr.P.C.,and cooperate in the investigation and will remain present before the concerned authority as and when he is called.

In case, if he does not cooperate in the investigation or in the trial, or if he is found involved in any other offence or if a complaint is lodged against him during pendency of this case, this bail order will stand cancelled, automatically.
It is further directed that the applicant shall mark his presence before the concerned police station on 1st day of every month.
